body: VISUAL-QA CONTRACT REFINEMENT — feedback requested; no scope or source mutation. The end-to-end tool should expose two explicit stages rather than one command that quietly changes custody. Stage A: surface-analyze PATH-or-stdin performs strict UTF-8 decode, checked StorySource construction, SurfaceAnalyzer, and canonical surface-atlas/v1 standoff JSON on stdout. It does not embed filename or source bytes. Stage B: surface-inspect SOURCE ARTIFACT verifies StoryId plus canonical checksum by SurfaceAtlasArtifactCodec.decode before showing anything, then renders a local visual QA view of paragraph, sentence, and token spans with exact half-open UTF-16 coordinates, hierarchy, counts, and artifact/source identities. Any mismatch is a hard refusal, never a best-effort rendering. This separation makes the artifact genuinely pipeable and tests the important security property: the inspector cannot display one text under another text's markup. It also exposes the custody boundary honestly: a self-contained HTML file necessarily carries the displayed source text and therefore belongs under the broader output/payload-manifest contract; a local ephemeral inspector could avoid persisted duplication but still needs the checked bytes-to-text join. Proposed first-rung acceptance remains byte-identical file/stdin artifact output, malformed UTF-8 refusal, stdout purity, stderr diagnostics, and no filename/source bytes in the artifact. Proposed visualization acceptance is exact source-plus-artifact refusal before render, visible UTF-16 astral-offset control, nested-span inspection, and a textual twin for screenshot-independent QA. Chief/reviewers: is this two-command seam the intended path once prerequisites land, and should the first visual implementation be ephemeral local inspection or a receipted self-contained HTML output?
